title: Polynitrogen Chemistry. Synthesis, Characterization, and Crystal Structure of Surprisingly Stable Fluoroantimonate Salts of N5+
authors: Vij A., Wilson W.W., Vij V., Tham F.S., Sheehy J.A., Christe K.O.

species.point_group: C2v (approximate -- real crystal geometry slightly asymmetric)
species.method: Single-crystal X-ray diffraction, N5+Sb2F11- salt (EXPERIMENTAL, not computational)
species.source_note: Table 2, p. ~6311; Table 1 gives full crystal data (monoclinic, C2/c, a=10.913(8) A, b=12.654(8) A, c=16.675(11) A, beta=104.715(18) deg)

bond_params.description: REAL experimental X-ray geometry of the N5+ cation (as its Sb2F11- salt), slightly asymmetric due to crystal packing (bonds/angles not perfectly C2v-symmetric: 1.102 vs 1.107, 1.303 vs 1.295). Only 2 of the 3 internal chain angles given explicitly in the paper's Table 2 (angle at N4, i.e. N3-N4-N5, not tabulated) -- do not assume it equals the N1-N2-N3 value given the observed asymmetry elsewhere.

species.suggested_build: chain2d (as bond_params fallback, since full Cartesian atom coordinates from the CIF are not reprinted as a table in the paper text itself, only derived bond lengths/angles)
species.notes: HIGH VALUE: this is a genuine EXPERIMENTAL structure (X-ray), not computational -- should likely take priority over any purely-DFT N5+ entry in the existing catalog for the 'reference' geometry of this species, even though it represents the same topology (duplicate by graph/formula/charge). Same species as N5.pdf's 'N5+_C2v_product' (computed: 1.111/1.302, close agreement) and referenced in N5-N6-abinitio.pdf. Flag this preference explicitly during dedup/report-writing: prefer experimental over computed when both represent the same topology.
